about:
I study autonomous AI systems as systems: how they are designed, how they behave in operation, how they fail, and how people keep oversight of them.

I have modeled complex systems for twenty years. I started in transportation network modeling and GIS. At the U.S. Federal Highway Administration I led technical components of the national Tour-Based Model System, a network model of long-distance travel, and managed a $1.5M federal research portfolio as a certified Contracting Officer's Representative. At Deloitte I delivered analytics and machine-learning engagements for public-sector clients. At AARP's Public Policy Institute I led the Livability Index, a decision-support system that scores U.S. neighborhoods from 50+ data sources across 7 domains.

Since 2024 I have designed and run QNFO, an autonomous research system of 44 live agents that draft, referee, revise, publish and correct papers, and I have published what it delivers, what it costs and where it fails (Operating the Quniverse Fleet), along with oversight methods for AI-assisted work (The Universal Ignorance Audit).

I am a systems researcher, not a software engineer. Open to research roles in autonomous and agentic AI systems, AI safety-adjacent work on evaluation, oversight and reliability, and systems research leadership. Earlier work is published under Brad Gudzinas.

experience.title: Founder and Systems Researcher
experience.company: QNFO (independent research on autonomous AI systems)
experience.description:
Designed and operate an autonomous research system on Cloudflare (44 live workers) that drafts, referees, revises, versions, publishes and corrects papers, with standing objectives, health checks and a failure ledger.

Reported how it behaves in operation: Operating the Quniverse Fleet (objectives, successes, failures, roadmap).

Designed oversight methods for AI-assisted work: The Universal Ignorance Audit; Epistemic Legibility in AI-Assisted Science.

Proposed JPCUB, a whole-system cost measure for computing (joules per correct answer), with an extension to stochastic and agentic LLM inference.
